learning_question: Which of the screen's 22 models, and five published signals they do not cover, rank next month's total returns reliably in both US universes (the hsr-v1 S&P 500 build and the hsr-mid-v1 mid-cap build) over 2000-2012? Does an equal-weight mix of only those beat the frozen screen's own model mix (its composite score) at the same breadth over 2013-2025, after costs?
n33_basis: N33 forbids tuning the frozen screen on history unless there is an explicit decision to run a controlled research experiment. The user asked for one on 2026-10-08 (test a much larger range of screening models and tailor the mix to the most reliable). This registration is that experiment: research only, fixed before data, never writes assign_signal, model weights, or any live knob.
inputs: Per universe: panel.csv.gz, daily.csv.gz, terminal_baseline.csv, the baseline signal cache (frozen composite score, plain value sort, screened names) and the dividend_units_fixed signal cache (model scores). All outside the repository.

holdout.reveal_rule: Revealed once, after the selection is committed and nothing in this file has changed. Later reveals are exploratory.

models.score: Each model's own score (0-1, higher is better) from the dividend_units_fixed signal cache: the models as the next screen epoch will score them once L571 is fixed. Scored with the frozen screen code; no model is edited.

published.definition: gross_margin x total_revenue / total_assets (latest trailing-twelve-month filing)
published.reference: Novy-Marx (2013), The other side of value

published.definition: shares_outstanding / shares_outstanding_prev - 1 (filing a year earlier); lower is better
published.reference: Pontiff and Woodgate (2008); Daniel and Titman (2006)

published.definition: total_assets / total_assets_prev - 1 (filing a year earlier); lower is better
adjusted close one month before the rebalance / adjusted close twelve months before - 1; each bar within 7 days of its date
published.reference: Jegadeesh and Titman (1993); value with momentum: Asness, Moskowitz and Pedersen (2013)

candidates.size: 22 models + 5 published signals = 27 candidates; no others are added after data

eligibility.statistic: Monthly rank IC: Spearman correlation, across the names screened that month with a fresh price, between the candidate's score and the total return to the next month-end (delisting exits at the last close, baseline haircut).
eligibility.rule: Kept only if, in every universe on the development window: the median share of names scored is at least min_median_coverage; at least min_months months have an IC; the lower bound of the mean IC (Newey-West, long_run_lag_months, z_search) is above zero; and the mean IC is above zero in each half of the window (first and second half of the months with an IC).

redundancy.rule: Order eligible candidates by mean IC averaged over universes (ties by id). Keep each in turn unless its mean monthly cross-sectional rank correlation with an already-kept candidate, averaged over universes, exceeds max_mean_rank_correlation.

mix.combine: Equal-weight mean of the kept candidates' cross-sectional percentile ranks. No fitted weights.
mix.book: Top top_share of names by mix score, equal weight, rebalanced monthly, charged the universe's cost per side on its turnover. A month with no names holds the equal-weight universe and is counted.

references.frozen_composite: The frozen screen's composite_score (baseline cache: the screen as it runs today), top 30%, built like the mix. The decision comparator: the same breadth isolates the mix from the tiering that hsr-v1 tests.
references.plain_value: The hsr-v1 plain value book (top 30% by positive earnings yield, equal weight, monthly, same costs), as in hrs-v1.
references.all_candidates: Equal-weight mix of every candidate that meets the coverage bar in every universe, without the IC filter. Context: does the selection beat averaging everything?
references.market: Cap- and equal-weighted screened universe. Context only.

costs.base_per_side: per universe (universes.*.cost_base_per_side): the hsr-v1 and hsr-mid-v1 base costs
costs.model: Each book pays cost x one-way turnover at each monthly rebalance, as the plain value book.

objective.definition: As hrs-v1: P(cumulative monthly log excess over the plain value book over H months > 0), with its lower bound.

pass_bars.mix_vs_frozen_composite: adds when the holdout 95% interval of the paired monthly difference (mix minus frozen composite, same months) is wholly above zero at base cost; costs when wholly below; otherwise inconclusive. Per universe.
pass_bars.verdict_vs_plain_value: pass when the holdout 36-month p_lower against the plain value book >= 0.5 at base cost; fail when p < 0.5; otherwise inconclusive.

overfitting.report: Per universe on the development window: PBO (CSCV) across the single-candidate top-30% books' excess over the plain value book, and the deflated Sharpe ratio of the mix against those trials.

reveal_order: Commit docs/data/historical_model_mix.json with the selection before any replay holdout is revealed: the replay's committed holdout series carry per-model holdout results. ftse-historical-replay run --reveal-holdout refuses until the selection is committed, and ftse-model-mix search refuses once either replay holdout is revealed. Reveal hms-v1 once, for both universes at base and stress cost.

decisions.mix_adds_in_both: mix_minus_frozen_composite is 'adds' in both universes at base cost and the mix does not fail against the plain value book in either: propose the kept candidates as the composite of a cold-start FTSE 350 library-screen paper twin with a frozen epoch (screen-code change, new replay registration). No live book changes on backtest evidence alone.
decisions.partial: Adds in one universe only, or adds but fails against the plain value book: no change. Record which size, and read FTSE 250 evidence separately before stage 4.
decisions.no_gain_over_frozen_mix: The tailored mix does not beat the frozen mix out of sample: keep the frozen mix. The development ranking was noise.
decisions.no_reliable_candidates: No candidate passes the development bar in both universes: keep the frozen mix; nothing is revealed but the references.
decisions.per_candidate_holdout: Holdout ICs per candidate are reported after the reveal, never used to re-select. A model that is reliably negative in both holdouts is a candidate for removal in the next simplification review, through the same twin path.

fixed_rules: Research only: no result here writes assign_signal, model weights, conviction, or any live knob (N33, N197).
No candidate, threshold, window, or rule changes after the search runs; changes open a new registration_id.
Selection uses the development window only and requires every universe; there are no fitted weights.
Only aggregates are committed: per-candidate IC summaries and monthly IC means, book-level monthly returns, and correlations between candidates. No per-name rows.
simplifications: Candidates are scored on the screened panel (names with fundamentals and a price), the same names as the plain value book.
Sector is today's classification (as in hsr-v1); models that rank within sector carry that small look-ahead.
The panel signals use the latest trailing-twelve-month filing and the filing a year earlier, filed at least 2 days before the rebalance.

amendments.change: sharadar_replay_adapter.py: tickers.table filter accepts the sharadar.com direct label 'fundamentals' as well as 'SF1'. mix_code_fingerprint re-frozen.
amendments.reason: Direct downloads label company rows 'fundamentals'; the old filter fell back to every row, so a fund or insider row reusing a ticker could replace the company. No search has run and no holdout has been revealed.

amendments.change: mix_code_fingerprint: hash file bytes with CRLF normalised to LF (Windows checkouts).
amendments.reason: Windows autocrlf made registration fingerprints fail before any licensed run could start; normalising newlines keeps Linux and Windows hashes aligned. No search has run and no holdout has been revealed.
